title: Constraint experiment weekly log - personal KPI sprint
content:
Goal: run a 3-week personal constraint experiment to reduce context switching, increase deep-work throughput, and make progress on two priority OKR outcomes.

Background / Why this feels important
- Last quarter I felt scattered: lots of partial tasks, multiple ping-pong PRs, a backlog of infra triage items.
- Quantitative pulse (rough): avg interruptions/day ~5.4, PRs merged/week ~1.2, focus hours (>=90min contiguous) ~3/week. Want to move these metrics measurably.

Hypotheses (micro):
1) If I limit active work-in-progress (WIP) to max 2 items, then PR merge rate will increase by reducing switching overhead.
2) If I batch shallow requests into a daily 30-minute sync window, then interruptions drop and focus hour increases.
3) If I prepare an explicit pre-flight checklist for infra triage, mean time to unblock reduces by 20%.

Experiment design (3 weeks)
- Week 0 (setup): identify top-2 outcome projects and write minimal success criteria. Create a triage checklist template.
- Weeks 1-3: enforce WIP <= 2, daily 30-min shallow-request window at 3pm, two deep-work blocks (90m) on M/W, Friday retro + unblock session.
- Metrics to track (manual): interruptions/day, contiguous focus hours/week, PRs merged/week, triage unblock time median.

Priority outcomes (personal OKRs draft)
- O1: Ship model-serving rollback automation for blue-green tests (tie to team OKR).
  - KR1: Merge feature branch and create rollout playbook by end of Feb.
  - KR2: Reduce manual rollback time from ~12m to <4m in playbook runbook trial.
- O2: Improve team observability for latency regressions in hosted API.
  - KR1: Add two targeted alert rules and a tracing runbook.
  - KR2: Run one canary with rollback automation integrated, ensure no customer-facing incidents.
- O3 (personal craft): Increase uninterrupted deep-work time to 8 hours/week across deep blocks.
  - KR1: Achieve avg 6+ contiguous hours/week by end of experiment.
  - KR2: Cut interruptions to <=2/day on average during weeks 2-3.

Daily routine (experiment constraints)
- Morning (09:00–10:00): triage + context prep for deep work; update pre-flight checklist.
- Deep block A (10:30–12:00): coding focused on O1.
- Lunch (12:00–13:00) — no Slack.
- Shallow window (15:00–15:30): batch all async messages, quick reviews.
- Deep block B (15:45–17:15): PR review or docs.
- End-of-day 17:30: quick log (3 lines): wins / blockers / plan for tomorrow.

Checklist: triage-preflight-template (notes to self)
- Repro steps or link to trace or flamegraph.
- Owner (who else needs to be looped).
- Minimal failing case and test harness.
- Hypothesis for root cause (1-2 lines).
- Quick rollback/mitigation possibility.

Weekly retro template (Friday)
- What worked: 
  - list 3 wins this week (small wins count).
- What didn't: 
  - interruptions that stopped deep work (time, source).
- Data snapshot: {interruptions/day avg, deep hours/week, PRs merged}. (I keep this manually in the sheet).
- Adjustments: what to change next week.

Preliminary notes / week 1 (observations)
- WIP cap felt constraining at first but forced prioritization; I moved one ancillary task to backlog and actually finished the main PR faster.
- Shallow window reduced quick pings but Slack threads still pulled me in before timer ended. Need a more explicit status message + DND gating.
- Deep blocks: achieved 3x 90m that week (not bad) -> feeling of momentum.
- Measured: interruptions/day ~3.7, deep hours/week ~4.5, PRs merged/week = 2.

Blockers / open questions
- How to message teammates so urgent customer issues still surface? Maybe a simple emergency tag ("urgent-release") that bypasses the shallow window.
- Is WIP cap 2 too low when small non-blocking reviews exist? Consider 1 major + 1 minor.
- Need to align with manager on expectations for shallow window — add to weekly 1:1 agenda.

Notes to self (formatting: quick, messy)
- Add a sentence to my calendar: "Shallow window active — please delay non-urgent pings".
- Automate triage checklist template into a reusable snippet in GH PR template (TODO: GH issue).
- Add measurement row to personal sheet: date / interruptions / deep-hours / PRs-merged / unblock-median.

Action items (short)
- A1 (today): post a status in #team-that-im-active-in-deep-work and set DND for deep blocks.
- A2 (this week): add triage checklist to repo PR template (create draft PR). Linked artifact: GitHub PR redwood/runtime#3245.
- A3 (by Friday): 1:1 with manager to align on shallow window policy.

Evaluation criteria (end of 3 weeks)
- Success if: interruptions/day reduced by >=30% from baseline AND deep-hours/week >=6 AND PRs merged/week improved by >=60%.
- Partial success: fewer interruptions OR steady improvement in deep-hours but needs another iter.

Reference links / quick refs
- Confluence: notes on focus experiments (personal) — placeholder, will link.
- JIRA: INFR-482 (rollback automation epic).
- GH PR draft: redwood/runtime#3245 (triage checklist insertion).

Freeform brain dump (scrappy)
- I keep defaulting to: finish the rollback automation first. That's the highest leverage for the week. If I get stuck, push for pairing to avoid spinning.
- Be generous with small wins: merging a doc or closing a discussion thread counts. Keeps morale up.
- If interruptions still high in week 2, consider an experimental "no-async-day" (one day/week silent except emergencies).

End log entry.
